story_text.value:
Hey, sometimes it's easier to just move around some buttons in an editor instead of waiting a minute for the AI result.

E.g. take a screenshot of your UI, cut out a button, move it around to see what it looks like.

Your AI can send HTML into the editor, or screenshots.

Then you can edit it, move things around, and your AI takes it from there.

I've made it free and open source. You can build on top of it or improve it.

title.value: Show HN: Free design canvas for your AI (open source)

story_text.value:
The idea is that whenever you have a server (which can be a remote server, but also just another process in the same machine, or even a sandboxed WASM module running in the same process as the renderer) they can send some simple messages and those can be turned into an interactive and reactive UI.

The renderer can be running in a terminal, a native app or basically anywhere else.

I guess it's somewhat like HTML, but purposefully much simpler so it can be implemented very easily, with built-in reactivity, no arbitrary code execution and a very limited set of components, so the server (mostly) can't influence _how_ things look on the client, only _what_.

title.value: Show HN: Hypereffect, a hypermedia protocol that renders reactive UIs everywhere
